15 min · 5 min → Bañuelo
4.Bañuelo
A Nasrid public bath from the 11th century, built along the Darro river at the base of the Alhambra hill. Five domed chambers — cold, tepid, and hot rooms — survive largely intact, with star-shaped skylights piercing brick vaults and horseshoe arches carried on Roman-era capitals reused from earlier buildings.

2.Dar al-Horra Palace
A rare surviving 15th-century Nasrid residential palace — home of Aisha al-Horra, mother of Granada's last sultan — arranged around a small courtyard pool. The quiet courtyard and intimate scale contrast with the Alhambra above.

From Hotel: 15 min · 13 min → Granada Cathedral
1.Granada Cathedral
A Renaissance cathedral raised over the city's former Great Mosque after the Reconquista — soaring white-and-gold nave and a monumental rounded apse. Diego de Siloé led the design from 1529; construction took 181 years.

2.Monasterio de San Jerónimo
A Renaissance monastery church built around Spain's largest gilded retablo, and burial place of Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba, "El Gran Capitán." The two-storey cloister and nave survive largely intact.

1 min · 2 min → Palacio de la Madraza
2.Palacio de la Madraza
Founded by Sultan Yusuf I in 1349, Granada's first madrasa served as a Quranic school before becoming the town hall after the Reconquista. The Baroque exterior conceals the original Nasrid oratory — its mihrab covered in 14th-century stucco tracery equal to anything inside the Alhambra.
Read more

Closed Saturday & Sunday
~30 min
Free
Oficios 14 · Centro
1 min · 2 min → Alcaicería
3.Alcaicería
A web of covered lanes occupying the site of the original Nasrid silk souk, rebuilt in Romantic-Moorish style after the 1843 fire. Lanterns, carved stucco, and tilework line the narrow passages; the market's silk trade has given way to ceramics, leather goods, and spice vendors alongside the Cathedral.
Read more
Open 24/7
~45 min
Calle Alcaicería · Centro
1 min · 2 min → Corral del Carbón
4.Corral del Carbón
Built around 1336 as a Nasrid caravanserai for the city's silk merchants, the Corral del Carbón is the oldest Islamic monument in Granada. The horseshoe gateway with its carved plaster frieze and the central courtyard survive intact; after 1492 the building became a coal yard, then a theatre.
Read more

~30 min

Day 5
From Hotel: 25 min · 8 min → Carmen de los Mártires
1.Carmen de los Mártires
A 19th-century villa on the Alhambra's western slope, surrounded by terraced gardens built over the site of a Carmelite convent where Christian prisoners were held during the Nasrid period. The grounds include an English romantic section, a French formal garden, a small lake, and a reconstructed Nasrid patio courtyard.
Read more
Daily 10:00am - 6:00pm
~1 hr
Free
Callejón de los Mártires · Alhambra
7 min → Fundación Rodríguez-Acosta
2.Fundación Rodríguez-Acosta
A Carmen-studio built between 1914 and 1930 for Granadan painter José María Rodríguez-Acosta, descending the Alhambra's southern slope across four terraced gardens. The subterranean galleries below house the Instituto Gómez-Moreno — Roman mosaics, Islamic ivories, pre-Columbian ceramics, and medieval sculpture.
Read more

13 min · 5 min → Huerta de San Vicente
3.Huerta de San Vicente
The García Lorca family's summer home from 1926 to 1936, where Federico wrote Blood Wedding, Yerma, and the Divan del Tamarit. The house is preserved as a working interior — Lorca's piano, desk, and personal library remain in place — surrounded by a small garden now absorbed into Parque García Lorca.

Local Tastes
Free Tapas
Every drink ordered at a bar in Granada arrives with a complimentary tapa, a tradition largely unique to Granada among major Spanish cities.
Taberna Salinas · Bar Minotauro · Taberna La Tana
Piononos
A small syrup-soaked rolled sponge cake invented in nearby Santa Fe, sold across Granada's pastry shops as the city's signature sweet.
Casa Ysla
Food Delivery
Glovo
Foreign number: accepted.
Glovo is the most widely used delivery platform in Granada, covering restaurants across the city centre, Realejo, and university areas with fast delivery and a broad restaurant selection.
glovoapp.com
Uber Eats
Foreign number: accepted.
Uber Eats covers central Granada with solid restaurant selection around the Albaicín and Realejo. Reliable for late-night orders when other platforms have fewer restaurants online.
ubereats.com

Getting Around
Cabify
Foreign number: not accepted — registration requires a Spanish or European phone number; use a local SIM or a VoIP number.
Cabify is the dominant ride-hailing option in Granada, covering the Albaicín, Sacromonte, and the broader city. Reliable at all hours and easy to book in advance for airport transfers to Aeropuerto Federico García Lorca.
cabify.com
Bolt
Foreign number: accepted.
Bolt operates across Granada with competitive fares and a solid driver pool — good alternative to Cabify, particularly in the city centre and around the university district. Foreign numbers from most countries are accepted at sign-up.
bolt.eu

Packing Checklist
Worth Knowing

The Alhambra's Nasrid Palaces ticket is timed to the minute and non-transferable — book the earliest morning slot available if flexibility matters, since afternoon slots sell out first in high season.

The walk down from Mirador de San Nicolás into Plaza Nueva at golden hour, past the sound of a distant guitar drifting out of a cave-house on Sacromonte, captures Granada's atmosphere better than any single monument on this itinerary.
